facts.fact: Under NFSA 2013, Priority Household (PHH) members are entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month
facts.quote: The Act entitles 35 kg of foodgrains per AAY Household per month, whereas 5 Kg of foodgrain per PHH Person per month.

facts.fact: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households, the poorest of the poor, are entitled to 35 kg per household (family) per month, regardless of family size
facts.quote: While AAY households, which constitute poorest of the poor are entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per family per month, priority households are entitled to 5 kg per person per month.
facts.note: 'Regardless of family size' is derived: the AAY entitlement is fixed per family, unlike the per-person PHH entitlement.

facts.fact: NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population
facts.quote: NFSA covers upto 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population under under Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) and priority households.
Identification of beneficiaries/households under NFSA is done by respective State/UT Government, which is required to frame its own criteria.

facts.fact: Since 1 January 2024 these foodgrains are free of cost under PMGKAY (for five years)
facts.quote: Free food grains (rice , wheat and coarse grains/millets) under PMGKAY for 5 years from 1.1.2024 will strengthen food security

summary: All confirmed: PHH 5 kg/person/month, AAY 35 kg/family/month (nfsa.gov.in), 75%/50% coverage, States identify beneficiaries, free under PMGKAY from 1.1.2024 (PIB).
